cues.text: A 48-year-old woman has had numbness and tingling in her left hand for a year.
It affects the radial three and a half digits, and her thenar eminence has wasted.
Tinel's sign is positive: tapping over her wrist sets off the tingling.
Phalen's sign is positive too, with both wrists held bent.
Together, these findings point to carpal tunnel syndrome.
Here, at the wrist, is the transverse carpal ligament.
Beneath it, the median nerve is compressed.
So compression of the median nerve causes her symptoms.
